result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, unmarked roadway that encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases crossing distances. While a sidewalk exists on one side, it is narrow and lacks continuity, and the overall infrastructure lacks dedicated safety features like bike lanes or mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: Excessive Roadway Width
hazards.description: The wide, unmarked travel lanes encourage higher vehicle speeds and increase the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic when crossing.

hazards.name: Inconsistent Sidewalk Infrastructure
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is narrow and appears to terminate or transition into a parking area, potentially forcing pedestrians into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the building frontage

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Markings
interventions.description: Apply clear lane markings and potentially add a bike lane or wider buffer to narrow the perceived travel lane and slow traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, wide, and ADA-compliant sidewalk on both sides of the street to provide a safe, dedicated path for pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and curb ramps. However, the presence of multiple driveway curb cuts for commercial parking and the lack of visible pedestrian signals or traffic calming measures increase risk for those crossing.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: Multiple curb cuts for the commercial parking lot create frequent points where vehicles cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk area in front of the brick commercial building

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation
interventions.description: Reduce the number of curb cuts to minimize conflict points between vehicles entering/exiting the parking lot and pedestrians on the sidewalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane roadway and expansive paved aprons that prioritize vehicle throughput. While a marked zebra crosswalk is present, the lack of signalization and the large turning radius create a high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The large radius at the corner allows vehicles to make right turns at high speeds across the pedestrian crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection where the crosswalk meets the sidewalk

hazards.name: Expansive Curb Cut/Apron
hazards.description: A very wide concrete apron for vehicle access creates a large area where pedestrians and vehicles may conflict without clear separation.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground, extending from the sidewalk area into the property

hazards.name: Long Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island or signalized protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, across the main roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to tighten the turning radius and shorten the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (PHB)
interventions.description: Install a signalized crossing to provide a protected interval for pedestrians to cross the wide roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous, well-maintained sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass buffer. While the physical separation is positive, the lack of street trees and the presence of a gated vehicle entrance introduce minor safety and comfort concerns.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A gated vehicle entrance crosses the sidewalk path, creating potential conflicts between pedestrians and entering/exiting vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image where the fence meets the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees in the grass buffer would provide shade, improve the aesthetic quality, and create a stronger sense of enclosure for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: If this is a common crossing point for the learning center, a marked mid-block crossing with appropriate signage should be considered.
